title: Ending a Patient Payment Plan by Cancellation or Payoff
content:
**Patient Payment Plans — Agreement terms: how a plan ends**

A plan ends in one of two ways other than default: the patient cancels it, or its balance reaches zero and it is paid off.

**1. Cancellation by the patient.** The patient may end an active or past-due plan at any time. Only the patient can end it; an agent cannot cancel it on the patient's behalf.

**2. Effect of cancellation.** On cancellation the whole remaining balance is released to the invoices, which return to the statement cycle at the next unused position. Installments already paid stay applied.

**3. Payoff.** A plan whose balance reaches zero is paid off, and where the term's payoff setting so provides, every invoice it carried is paid.

**4. No fee.** Neither cancellation nor payoff carries a fee.

**5. Credit reporting.** A balance on a current plan is never reported to credit bureaus.

## Which plans the patient can cancel

| Plan status | Patient may cancel |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Past due | Yes |
| Pending acceptance, defaulted, paid off, cancelled | Not under this clause |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A patient on an active 9-Month Payment Plan has paid four installments of 50.00 and cancels with 250.00 remaining. The 250.00 is released to the plan's invoices, which return to the statement cycle at their next unused position; the 200.00 already paid stays applied. No fee is charged.
- A relative calls to cancel the patient's plan. The plan is ended only by the patient.
- A plan's last installment brings its balance to zero. The plan is paid off and, on every term, the invoices it carried are paid.
